summary.headline: Ashok Leyland FY26 revenue hit INR44,007 crore (+13.6%) with Q4 EBITDA margin at 14.6%; management flags steel-led commodity pressure in Q1 FY27.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 CV volume of 220,437 units (including defense) and record FY26 revenue, PAT and cash surplus. Q4 revenue was INR14,161 crore (+19% YoY) and EBITDA INR2,066 crore (14.6% margin), though operating leverage was weak due to performance bonus provisions. Management said Q4 gross margin improved 80 bps despite commodity headwinds, helped by ~1% price hikes in January and value-engineering/e-sourcing savings. Outlook is cautious: May demand is holding, but diesel availability and steel costs are the main near-term concerns for Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Q4 +80 bps YoY; FY +10 bps YoY
up more than INR1,650 crore YoY

segments.name: MHCV domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 trucks 105,905 units (30.2% share) and buses 20,840 units (34.1% share). Industry MHCV volume grew 12% for FY26 and 21.5% in Q4.

segments.name: LCV domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 21,801 units (+23% YoY), VAHAN share 12.8% (+90 bps). FY26 volume 74,322 units (+12%), a record, with share 12.7% (+80 bps).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 18,082 units (+18.5%), a record. Q4 volume 5,322 units, marginally down YoY on March logistics issues; FY26 export revenue about INR3,200 crore. Q4 export revenue INR1,100 crore vs INR825 crore.

segments.name: Spares / aftermarket and Power Solutions
segments.commentary: Domestic aftermarket revenue +11.2% in Q4 and +9.5% for FY26. FY26 spares about INR3,800 crore (Q4 INR1,060 crore vs INR950 crore); Power Solutions about INR1,400 crore, up 16.4%.

segments.name: Defense
segments.commentary: FY26 defense revenue about INR1,200 crore including subsidiary ALDS (standalone about INR800 crore), up ~20%. Q4 defense revenue INR275 crore vs INR170 crore. Order book above INR1,500 crore, executed over 1 to 3 years.

segments.name: Switch Mobility (EV)
segments.commentary: Reached net profit in FY26 (PAT about INR100-plus crore). Delivered 1,530 e-buses (+238%) and 1,600 e-LCVs (+56%); order book about 1,600 units.

segments.name: Hinduja Leyland Finance / Hinduja Housing Finance
segments.commentary: HLF AUM about INR59,000 crore (+24%), PAT INR491 crore (+20%). HHF AUM about INR16,000 crore (+15%), PAT INR387 crore (+4%). Consolidated net NPA about 1.4%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex planned at INR750-1,000 crore, versus INR1,000 crore in FY26.

Investment in subsidiaries to depend on need: HLF, HHF and OHM are named as likely to require funds; Switch is self-sufficient. Repaid about GBP30 million of the GBP80 million Optare loan to Switch UK.
Q1 FY27 price increase of about 1-1.5% from April 1; sustainability for the full quarter is uncertain.
Q1 FY27 commodity costs (mainly steel) are expected to rise significantly; management declined to give a quantified range.
Management expects Q1 FY27 industry CV performance to be better than Q1 FY26, but declined to give full-year industry growth guidance.
Export dispatches may dip in Q1 FY27 due to logistics issues; RAK plant is being ramped back to 100% utilisation over a few weeks.
Reverse merger of HLF with NBL Ventures expected to complete within this or the next quarter.
Battery pack plant at Pillaipakkam: construction to start in 8-10 weeks, production start targeted for Q2 FY27. PLI update expected in 4-5 months.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR1,050 crore, mostly for new products, future technology, alternate powertrains and EVs; Q4 capex INR203 crore.
Network at FY26 end: 2,104 touchpoints (1,159 MHCV, 945 LCV), with 100+ added each in MHCV and LCV and over 45% of additions in North and Northeast.
Battery pack plant (greenfield, Pillaipakkam near Chennai) groundbroken in Q4; phased plan: pack first, then non-captive pack, then cell manufacturing.
RE status 77% (FY25: 69%); Tamil Nadu plants at 91% RE100.
Newly launched HIPPO high-HP tractors and TAURUS tippers began dispatch only in Feb-Mar FY26 (a few hundred units); meaningful impact expected from Q2 FY27 in tippers and tractor-trailers.
demand_pricing: Industry MHCV volume grew 21.5% YoY in Q4 and 12% for FY26. Growth was driven by GST rate cut of about 10% from October, and fleet replacement with an aged fleet at an all-time high.
May 2026: no significant slowdown in MHCV or LCV demand, but diesel availability and price concerns are affecting logistics in some pockets. Diesel has risen about INR7 so far.
Retail is about 55-60% of heavy-duty truck demand; the rest is fleet. Retail is a much higher share in ICV and LCV.
Mix: ICV demand outpaced heavy-duty trucks, which is a margin-mix headwind. Management expects tipper, multi-axle and trip-trailer (mining/infrastructure) segments to grow fastest.
Export demand in GCC, Africa and SAARC is holding at retail level despite higher oil prices.
Non-vehicle revenue demand continues into Q1 FY27 per management; no dip seen so far.
Price increases: none taken Oct-Mar; about 1-1.5% taken from April 1 across product categories.
Management expects the industry to take multiple price increases during FY27 given cost inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What demand signals are being seen after fuel price hikes, and what is the FY27 outlook for MHCV and exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand is resilient, with no significant slowdown in May. Diesel availability is the issue in some pockets. Exports may dip in Q1 due to logistics, but demand is not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: How much price was taken, and what is the commodity pressure and Q1 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1% price hike in January, sustained through Q4. Q4 cost increases were offset by value engineering and e-sourcing savings. For Q1, about 1-1.5% price increase, with significant steel-led commodity inflation. Management declined to quantify the range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income rise and what are capex and investment plans for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income increase reflects returns on surplus fund investments. FY27 capex is INR750-1,000 crore. Subsidiary investments depend on need, with HLF, HHF and OHM likely to require funds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is net cash so much higher than December, and what are the non-vehicle revenue figures?
qa_highlights.answer: The jump is seasonal working capital, with payables peaking in April-May. Net cash is up over INR1,650 crore YoY. FY26 spares about INR3,800 crore, Power Solutions about INR1,400 crore, exports about INR3,200 crore, and defense about INR1,200 crore including subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give a range for FY27 industry growth in a downside case?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to estimate. It said demand is resilient, and any Q1/Q2 dip could convert to pent-up demand in Q3/Q4. Q1 FY27 is expected to be better than Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Cross-functional teams are reviewing opex line by line for savings. Recovery is possible only partly; if commodity costs rise sharply, the margin impact will be significant.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no operating leverage in Q4 on staff and other costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Performance bonus provisions for executives were booked only in Q4, after thresholds were met, and commodity costs also rose. Q4 gross margin still improved 80 bps QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did market share appear to decline, and what is the impact of new launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says MHCV share has risen over FY22-FY26. Some share was lost in higher-HP tractors and tippers due to delayed launches. The new models are expected to lift share from Q2 FY27.

risks_watch: Steel and other commodity inflation in Q1 FY27 with limited pass-through; recovery depends on price hikes and cost savings.
Diesel availability and price increases affecting fleet operator uptime and ICV/LCV demand.
Export logistics disruption and RAK plant utilisation recovery.
Mix shift toward ICV from heavy-duty trucks, which is margin-dilutive.
Funding needs of HLF, HHF and OHM, plus the battery plant and PLI thresholds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and on the baseline demand, but cautious on FY27. The management is noticeably evasive on quantifying commodity pressure and industry growth ranges, saying it is too early to estimate.
key_quotes: Despite commodity headwinds, we could maintain and even improve our gross margins.
So we do not want to sacrifice on that view or that demand which might come up later.
Now how much we will grow with respect to Q4 and Q3 and how much we will grow with respect to last year is something which remains to be seen.
It's too early to give a range or a number, Kapil.
I would have loved to give you an estimate, but I wouldn't hazard a guess here because I'm really shooting in the dark.
In May, we are not seeing any significant slowdown, both on the MHCV and LCV side.
